A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Taurus is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **Taurus** is "a foot-operated analog synthesizer" by **Moog Music**; the Taurus I was made from **1975** to 1981 (Wikipedia, "Moog Taurus").
- You play it on **pedals**, like an organ's, so your hands stay free for keyboards or guitar (Wikipedia).
- The Taurus III of 2010 closely follows the first one (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- **Two oscillators**, both sawtooth; **Beat** detunes the second one (Taurus 205A manual, PDF pp. 3, 6).
- A 24 dB low-pass **filter** with its own contour: attack, decay and amount (manual, PDF pp. 3-6).
- **Glide** slides from note to note (manual, PDF p. 5).
- It plays one note at a time.

This is the Taurus panel from [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). ## Guided tour

Each step loads the pedal-bass example and changes one knob.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="taurus-bass" data-set="{&quot;beat&quot;:0,&quot;mixB&quot;:0}"><p><b>One oscillator.</b> Oscillator B off. Listen: a plain bass.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="taurus-bass"><p><b>Add Beat.</b> Oscillator B on and slightly detuned. Listen: it wobbles and gets fatter.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="taurus-bass" data-set="{&quot;cAmt&quot;:0}"><p><b>No filter contour.</b> Contour amount at 0. Listen: dull, no movement.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="taurus-bass" data-set="{&quot;cAmt&quot;:9,&quot;emph&quot;:6}"><p><b>More contour and Emphasis.</b> Listen: each note opens with a "bwow".</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="taurus-bass" data-set="{&quot;glideOn&quot;:true,&quot;glide&quot;:6}"><p><b>Glide.</b> Listen: notes slide into each other.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Moog Taurus":

- used by Genesis, Yes, Rush, Tool and Dream Theater
